nippert-stadium: The university policy linked by UC athletics allows service animals with visitor handlers in campus public-accommodation areas, subject to its stated exceptions. Contact with Accessibility Resources before visiting is encouraged, not required; the policy says service animals need no identifying vest or university certification/registration.
Visitors. Service Animals accompanied by a visitor Handler may be brought into areas of public accommodation on campus, unless otherwise prohibited by this Policy

While not required, Handlers are encouraged to partner with Accessibility Resources (for students and visitors) or Human Resources (for employees) before bringing a Service Animal into University facilities of public accommodation

Service Animals are not required to:
Wear a vest or other identification that indicates they are a Service Animal.
Handlers may consider having the animal wear some type of commonly recognized identification symbol identifying the animal as a Service Animal, while not disclosing the disability.
Be certified by or registered with the University.
Employee and student Handlers may consider obtaining a free University ID Card for their Service Animal by contacting Accessibility Resources (students) or Human Resources (employees).

UC’s linked animal policy places animal care and welfare with the handler. Handlers unable to collect and dispose of waste must arrange assistance themselves, and should have a local emergency contact able to care for the animal off campus if the handler becomes unable to do so. No venue-provided animal-care service is established.
The cost of care, arrangements, and responsibilities for the well-being of an animal are the sole responsibility of the Handler.

Handlers are required to clean up after and properly dispose of a Service Animal or Emotional Support Animal’s waste in a safe and sanitary manner in outdoor trash receptacles. Handlers who are not physically able to pick up and dispose of animal waste are responsible for making all necessary arrangements for assistance.

Handlers should ensure that their Service Animal or Emotional Support Animal has a care plan in place (a local emergency contact) in the event of an emergency where the Handler may be incapacitated or otherwise unable to care for the animal.
The local emergency contact must be able to care for the animal off University property while the Handler is incapacitated or otherwise unable to care for the animal.

cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum: The standard Great American Ball Park Tour checks in at the museum lobby, covers about three-quarters of a mile and lasts about 75–90 minutes, with exposure to the weather. The Reds describe it as wheelchair- and stroller-accessible and offer complimentary wheelchairs for guests who have difficulty walking. Confirm a specific route, transfer needs and rest opportunities before booking.
Guests check in for tours located in the lobby of the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum.
This is a walking tour (approximately 3/4 mile) that is subject to the elements, so we suggest wearing comfortable footwear and weather-appropriate attire.
Tours are wheelchair and stroller accessible. The Reds Hall of Fame provides complimentary wheelchairs for guests who may have difficulty walking.

For the standard ballpark tour, all ticket sales are final and non-refundable. The itinerary can change without notice and some locations may be closed on a given tour; do not assume a particular stop will be included.
Please note that the tour itinerary and locations are subject to change without notice. All locations may not be open for every tour.
All ticket sales are final and non-refundable.
